Researchers at the institute have developed a new reference material for evaluating the performance of protective fabrics, a step that could help strengthen the domestic supply chain for firefighting gear. The material is a standardized textile with precisely controlled properties, allowing laboratories to check whether their instruments are producing consistent results. Until now, manufacturers and testing labs have relied on a patchwork of in-house standards that made comparisons difficult. “Having a common yardstick matters,” said one of the project leads. “If two labs measure the same fabric and get different answers, nobody can trust either result.” The material will be distributed to participating laboratories later this year, and the team plans to publish a detailed protocol so that others can reproduce the tests. Results from an interlaboratory study will be released in the spring.
